objective: At the owner's request ('Yes, let's continue', approving BEYOND-TWO-20261101-001's recommendation): does composing like cycles force rigid selection? Test the remaining cycle-composing laws (coset laws of Z4, Z_(p^k), S3, D_p; the simple Mal'tsev laws on three values) for global failures on regular substrates that keep a knot after a line is removed, and prove rigidity where it holds. If a non-rigid global failure exists, build from it (by blurring) a law that composes like cycles, selects globally, counts hard and keeps a knot inside its selected spaces. No time constraints.
status: Complete 2026-11-01: composing like cycles does not force rigid selection, but selection spends the top layer. Over fields every global failure is rigid (corank 1), as are blurred laws, S3 and D_p; over Z_(p^k) with k >= 2 global failures keep knots (signed Z4 on a 6-point 4-regular substrate after every removal; at three places from 9 points). Over any finite chain ring a global failure leaves, after any removal, solutions whose top layer is one line, so kept knots have at most one full-range variable and hide at most k - 1 digits. Blurred signed Z4 on five values composes like cycles, selects globally, counts #P-complete and keeps knots below its top layer; at two values composing like cycles forces rigidity while the knot keeps knots; next: the top layer for every law that composes like cycles (2/3)
stop_rule: Stop when rigidity is proved for the families where it holds and a non-rigid global failure is either exhibited (verified independently) or excluded on the bounded families; record the bridge only with its verified properties.
title: Does composing like cycles force rigid selection?
